evals.prompt: Coordinate steps 2 to 4 of docs/specs/session.md. I will review on GitHub.
evals.expected_output: Reads AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, the ADRs and the spec, checks its criteria are signed off, opens the ledgers, holds back any step whose requirements lack criteria, fills template-phase.md per ready step with its criteria and behaviour target, and starts one fresh worker per independent step.
expectations: Reads AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, docs/adr and docs/specs/session.md before filling any brief, and checks the status line reads criteria signed off
Creates or reads units.tsv and decisions.tsv in the notes folder and writes a row per started step
A step serving a requirement with no criterion is not started and is handed to the criteria skill
Each brief follows template-phase.md with every section filled, including Read first, Decisions already made, Not asked for now and Done means
Each brief's Done means carries the step's criteria as written and a behaviour target of live-verified when any criterion is a drive check, unit-only when any is a test check, otherwise none

Each brief names the model tier, the coordinating tier with its model and effort, not whatever model the coordinator runs on, one up when the step is subtle or security-sensitive, and the Standing orders block is copied from AGENTS.md word for word
Each worker is a fresh session in its own worktree, not a fork of the coordinator, and the coordinator edits no source file
Each brief's Owns lists the step's status line and the Status cells of its criteria rows in the spec, so the worker can record progress as implement requires without editing anything else in the spec

evals.prompt: Worker says: PR 42 is ready, head a9c1f3e, make validate exit 0 on a clean checkout.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks the claim against gh pr view and origin/<branch> before moving the row to ready, binds the PR monitor once, then fills template-review.md and starts a fresh reviewer session that is not the worker session, choosing the review tier first and then the other model family at that tier where present. The brief requires the gate on a detached checkout, a base-against-candidate probe, design and maintainability at the same weight as correctness, guard-deletion sampling, P1 to P3 findings with file:line, one COMMENT review and never an approval.
expectations: Runs gh pr view and compares headRefOid with the reported sha before the units.tsv row moves to ready

Checks that every criterion in the brief has its own row in the worker's verify block before the behaviour row, with the brief's command, an exit code and pass, or met for an inspection; a criterion with no row or one reading not run goes back to the worker as one line naming the criterion, and the row does not move to ready
The review brief carries the criteria and requires each command run on the detached checkout and checked against the worker's row, with a failed or missing criterion as a P1 naming it

The review brief keeps the detached worktree from the gate through the criteria checks and the guard sample and removes it only in its Cleanup section, so no step runs in a checkout an earlier step removed

The reviewer is a separate fresh session, not the worker session and not the coordinator itself; its tier is chosen first, strong, or top when the step is subtle or security-sensitive, and it runs on the other model family from the coordinator's at that tier when present, otherwise on the coordinator's

The review brief follows template-review.md and names the detached gate, the correctness probe, the equal-weight design and maintainability lenses, guard-deletion sampling and the P1 to P3 table with file:line
The brief says to post one COMMENT review and never approve or request changes
A decisions.tsv row of kind verdict is written when the reviewer reports

evals.prompt: Reviewer verdict on PR 42: after fixes. F1 P2 packages/core/src/verify.ts:42 secret compared with ===, F2 P2 guard at src/parse.ts:88 survives deletion, F3 P3 naming.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not fix anything itself. It decides whether the fix needs state that lives only in the worker session; if not, it starts a fresh fix session with the original phase brief plus the findings consolidated, standing orders pasted verbatim, one commit per finding, no weakened tests, PR kept draft until verify passes on the pushed head and no check has failed. It logs a relay row in decisions.tsv, and after the fix the same reviewer flow re-checks the new head, bounded at three rounds.
expectations: The coordinator makes no code edit in response to the findings
The relay or fresh-session choice is stated with the reason, and a decisions.tsv row of kind relay records it
The fix brief carries the standing orders verbatim, the review file path, one commit per finding, no weakened tests and the draft-until-gated rule
The re-check is a reviewer pass on the new head that classifies F1, F2 and F3 as fixed, not fixed or no longer applicable with a line each
The fix loop is bounded at three rounds, after which the row moves to blocked and the owner gets the open findings
A round after one whose findings came back not fixed starts a fresh session one tier above the last round's

evals.expected_output: The agent prints units.tsv as a table, one line per step with its state, PR and head, corrects any row that disagrees with gh pr view in the file first, and lists the parked questions the owner still owes. Nothing comes from recollection.
expectations: The answer is read from units.tsv and decisions.tsv, with the command shown
Each step appears with its state, PR number and head SHA
A row that disagrees with gh pr view is corrected in the file before the answer is given
Parked ADR-tier questions are listed as lettered options still owed by the owner

evals.prompt: Worker on step 3 asks: should the session token live in the signed cookie or in the store? Also, should the helper be called parseClaims or readClaims?
evals.expected_output: The agent sorts the two forks. The token location is a data-model decision, so it goes to the owner as lettered options with a recommendation, the row is parked, and the other rows keep draining. The helper name is below the ADR tier, so the agent decides it against the glossary, writes a decisions.tsv row of kind fork with the reason, tells the worker, and names it in the next report.
expectations: The token location is presented to the owner as lettered options with a recommendation first and is not decided by the agent
The step 3 row moves to parked while the other rows continue
The helper name is decided by the agent with a reason tied to CONTEXT.md and relayed to the worker
A decisions.tsv row of kind fork records the name decision and the parked question

evals.prompt: Reviewer verdict on PR 42: merge as is. Gate green on a9c1f3e detached, review in review-pr42.md. Step 3 is the next ready step.
evals.expected_output: The agent sends the owner one line with the verdict and its evidence, moves the units.tsv row to merge-ready, starts the step 3 worker at once without waiting for the merge, and in Claude Code schedules one recurring merge check for the frontier with CronCreate when none exists, whose prompt runs gh pr view on every merge-ready row and Step 9 on each MERGED one. It never runs gh pr merge and never arms auto-merge.
expectations: One line to the owner carries the verdict, the review file, the gated head and its exit code
The units.tsv row for PR 42 moves to merge-ready
The step 3 worker is started before PR 42 is merged, as a fresh session in its own worktree
A single CronCreate job covers the merge frontier, with a prompt that checks every merge-ready row with gh pr view and runs the cleanup for each MERGED one, and no gh pr view loop runs in the session
No gh pr merge and no auto-merge

evals.prompt: Coordinate docs/specs/billing.md. Its status line reads draft.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to start any worker because the criteria aren't signed off, and offers the criteria skill.
expectations: Reads the spec's status line before filling any brief
Starts no worker and fills no brief
Offers the criteria skill to write and sign off the criteria

evals.prompt: Coordinate step 3 of docs/specs/handbook.md. It serves R5 (the README explains setup), whose only criterion C5.1 is an inspection of the README. The criteria are signed off.
evals.expected_output: Fills the brief with C5.1 and a behaviour target of none, since no criterion is a drive or test check, so the worker is judged on the criteria alone and not sent back for lacking a unit test.
expectations: The brief's behaviour target reads none, with the criteria alone deciding, not unit-only or live-verified
When checking the worker's report, a met C5.1 with no behaviour test is accepted rather than sent back for a missing test

evals.prompt: Worker says PR 51 is ready. Step 4 rotates the session signing key, so the brief marked it security-sensitive. The Codex plugin is installed in this Claude session.
evals.expected_output: The agent picks the review tier first, top because the step is security-sensitive, then the family, Codex because it is present, and the review brief names Codex, its strongest model and its highest reasoning effort explicitly rather than whatever Codex defaults to.
expectations: The review tier is top, decided from the step being security-sensitive before the family is chosen
The reviewer runs through Codex, not on Claude, because the plugin is present
The review brief's Model tier line names the host, the model and the reasoning effort for top on Codex, and does not leave effort to a default

evals.prompt: Re-check on PR 42 after round 1: F1 not fixed. The worker's session is halfway through a rebase with a staged resolution in src/verify.ts and an untracked src/verify.test.ts, both inside the phase's Owns. The unignored notes folder docs/plans/2026-11-04-coordinate-auth/ and an unrelated stray.txt are also untracked.
evals.expected_output: Escalation wins over the worker-state route. The handover snapshots only the Owns paths through a throwaway index against the pushed head, writes round-1.patch, records the tree id and the rebase's onto, and only then aborts the rebase. The escalated session proves the patch in a throwaway worktree, rebases its own clean checkout onto onto, carries the snapshot's resolution and new test over, and names any file that still differs from the snapshot with its cause.
expectations: Round 2 runs in a fresh session one tier above round 1's, not in the worker by relay
The handover uses a throwaway index with git add limited to the Owns paths, never git add -A, so neither the notes folder nor stray.txt is in the patch and the artifact hook does not refuse it
The snapshot runs before the rebase is aborted, the rebase is never finished, and a failed snapshot line leaves the rebase untouched
The handover reports the pushed head, the patch path, the tree id and the rebase's onto commit
The escalated session applies the patch in a throwaway worktree and compares git write-tree with the tree id, stopping on a mismatch, while its own checkout stays clean

It rebases its own checkout of the pushed head onto onto, the rebase starts without an uncommitted-changes refusal, and src/verify.ts ends with the snapshot's resolution and src/verify.test.ts is present
Any file in the Owns paths that still differs from the tree id afterwards is named in the report with the replayed commit that changed it
A decisions.tsv relay row records the route, the tier and why
